items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Green, William and myself, I was known as Johnson, were going from place to place doing our numbers

ctx.x: Then another cornet player came to Cincinnati from New Orleans and he used to advertise for the Lincoln Theatre by playing on a wagon which was pulled around town by a horse, and this fellow used to play alone. I would follow him for blocks whenever he came on the street where I lived.

Some other musical events used to happen on my street. Were were living on Kenyon Avenue and just across the street from my house, there were two brothers whose family name was Johnson. The oldest must have been about 22 and the other 18 years old and they both played piano. During the summer they had their front door open and would play for hours. I used to sit on their steps and listen to them and was very unhappy when my mother would call me to run an errand for her.

Other people used to stop and listen to these two young men play. The oldest one was better than the younger one and I suppose the reason was that he had more experience, but the younger one was no amateur although I found out that they did not read music. There were many pianists in those days that did not read music but had a natural talent for that instrument. They made their living playing for parties most of the time.
